text: Fixing one bug isn't the same as proving the whole platform trustworthy. This lesson builds a formal, repeatable reconciliation that traces a number from the dashboard all the way back to the original CSV.

We deliberately pick four different kinds of days -- an ordinary day, a day with returns, a day with employee discounts, and the Store 11 night from last lesson's fix -- because a check that only ever runs against simple, clean days doesn't prove the edge cases work.
Four hops get compared for each test case: the raw CSV by hand, the staging table, the warehouse, and the published dashboard. Each one has to tie out exactly to the one before it.
Every hop that matches confirms the whole chain; a hop that doesn't tells you exactly where the bug actually lives -- Extract, Transform, Load, or the DAX itself.
All four test cases tie out exactly, including the Store 11 fix. This becomes a standing line in UAT sign-off, not a one-time proof. Next: a real performance problem, and how it got fixed.
